newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana wants limited ivory trade.
newsitem.headline: Botswana wants limited ivory trade.

text.p: Botswana said on Wednesday it would ask at an international meeting next week on protecting endangered species to be allowed to undertake limited and controlled trade in stockpiled ivory with one buyer.
"Funds from the trade will be used to establish wildlife management programmes that will eventually include culling," said George Kgoroba, minister for commerce and industry.
Botswana wants to immediately sell 25 tonnes of stockpiled ivory. A Japanese buyer has been identified who has agreed not to re-export the ivory, nor products made from it.

Ivory trade is banned, but Botswana and other southern African countries are to make the case for a limited, controlled trade at the meeting of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) that opens on June 9 in Zimbabwe.
Wildlife experts say Botswana had 79,000 elephants in 1995, a population growing at five percent a year, and that available habitat in the country could support only 33,000 elephants.
Kgoroba said Botswana had received many expressions of support for its proposal, but also many letters decrying the action.
"The letters against us are from individuals in Britain and Europe who do not understand our situation," Kgoroba said.
"At least seven villagers have been killed or maimed by elephants this year."
